prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals

Health and social care
- Increase NHS operating spend by £8bn in year one, rising to £28bn by 2030, plus at least £20bn capital over five years.
- Reduce waiting lists; rapid GP access; guaranteed NHS dentistry with funding rising to £3bn/year by 2030.
- Invest in primary care (up to £1.5bn/year by 2030) and £2bn capital; expand community diagnostics.
- Support fair pay settlements and staff retention; back junior doctor pay restoration.
- National Cancer Control Plan; access to evidence-based mental health therapies within 28 days; counsellors in every school/college.
- Legal reform to allow assisted dying with safeguards; end new HIV cases by 2030.
- Introduce free personal care; invest £20bn/year in social care; create career structures and fair pay for carers; £3bn extra for children’s social care.
- Uplift disability benefits by 5% and expand support for disabled people and carers.

Housing and planning
- Build 150,000 new social homes per year; end “right to buy”; empower rent controls; end no-fault evictions.
- Retrofit and resilience: £29bn for home insulation to EPC B over 10 years (first five years funded), £9bn for low‑carbon heat, £7bn for overheating adaptation, £4bn for public buildings.
- Mandate Passivhaus‑equivalent standards; require solar and low‑carbon heat in new builds; upgrade private rentals to EPC C.
- Reform planning to link development with services, protect green spaces, reuse materials, and account for whole‑life carbon.

Energy and climate
- No new oil/gas licences; introduce a rising carbon tax to £500/t within 10 years.
- Target ~70% electricity from wind by 2030; end barriers to onshore wind; capacity aims by 2035: 80GW offshore wind, 53GW onshore, 100GW solar.
- Expand grid, storage, interconnectors; promote community ownership; regulate biofuels; end subsidies for imported biomass; cease new nuclear and phase out existing plants.

Economy and tax
- Invest an average £40bn/year in a green transition (energy, retrofits, rail, public transport, active travel, industry decarbonisation, water/sewage, nationalisations).
- Bring railways, water companies and major energy retailers into public ownership.
- Wealth tax: 1% on assets >£10m and 2% >£1bn; align capital gains and investment income with earned income; remove NI upper earnings cap; reform inheritance and property taxes; revalue Council Tax; long-term move toward Land Value Tax.
- Windfall taxes on oil/gas and banks; targeted VAT changes; stronger HMRC resourcing and anti‑avoidance measures; borrow to invest.

Work and welfare
- Charter of Workers’ Rights; day‑one rights; repeal restrictions on industrial action.
- Minimum wage £15/hour; 10:1 maximum pay ratios; full rights for platform workers; support a four‑day week.
- Welfare: +£40/week to Universal Credit/legacy benefits; end five‑week wait and two‑child cap; maintain pension uprating; raise Carer’s Allowance; scrap bedroom tax; end sanctions; long‑term path to Universal Basic Income.

Nature, animals, food and farming
- Rights of Nature Act; protect 30% of land and sea by 2030; increase DEFRA budget by £1.5bn; public ownership of water; Clean Air Act; rewet peat; expand marine protections; restrict destructive fishing.
- Commission on Animal Protection; ban blood sports; end factory farming practices; strengthen welfare standards.
- Nearly triple farm support to shift to nature‑friendly farming; reduce pesticides; expand horticulture; free school meals for all children and breakfast clubs; food education and local food partnerships.

Education
- Schools: £8bn extra (including £2bn for teacher pay); £2.5bn/year to fix and maintain buildings; broaden curriculum; abolish high‑stakes tests and OFSTED; bring academies under local control; charge VAT on private school fees (with SEND exemptions); expand SEND funding by £5bn; restore school nurses and provide counsellors.
- Post‑16/FE: £3bn more for sixth forms; £12bn for skills and lifelong learning; restore Education Maintenance Allowance.
- Higher education: scrap tuition fees; restore grants; address pension funding pressures.

Transport
- By end of parliament: £10bn/year subsidy for rail/bus; £19bn over five years for public transport, electrification, cycling/walking; public ownership of rail; local control of buses; free bus travel for under‑18s; £2.5bn/year for active travel.
- Oppose new roads; consider road pricing; restore fuel‑duty escalator.
- End sales of new petrol/diesel cars by 2027; phase out on-road use by 2035; £5bn/year EV scrappage; rapid charging rollout; default 20mph in built‑up areas.
- Aviation: frequent‑flyer levy; ban domestic flights where rail <3 hours; apply carbon tax to kerosene; halt airport expansion; support worker transition.

Democracy, rights and migration
- Proportional representation; replace House of Lords with elected chamber; votes at 16; repeal voter‑ID; strengthen transparency and party finance rules; expand devolution; defend human rights law; restore legal aid; support gender recognition reform.
- Migration and asylum: end “hostile environment”; remove minimum income rules for family visas; safe routes; right to work while claims are decided; abolish NRPF; simplify visas and charge at cost; free NHS access for visa holders; limit detention to public‑safety cases; voting rights for visa‑holding residents; restructure Home Office functions.

Culture, media, digital
- £5bn over five years for community arts, culture and sport; protect local venues; VAT exemptions for cultural events; support local media; cap media market share at 20%; implement Leveson recommendations.
- Digital Bill of Rights; strong data protection; precautionary AI regulation; protect creators’ IP; facilitate EU touring for artists.

Justice and policing
- Restore trust in policing; end routine stop‑and‑search and facial recognition; expand restorative justice; presumption against custodial sentences under two years.
- Invest £11bn over the parliament in the justice system; recruit more judges; tackle domestic abuse and violence against women and girls; decriminalise sex work; fund youth services and violence reduction units.

Foreign policy and security
- Uphold international law; support Ukraine; reform European security architecture; aim to rejoin the EU (via customs union first), restore free movement and Erasmus; reform trade deals to remove investor‑state tribunals.
- Sign the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons and dismantle nuclear arsenal; work within NATO while advocating reforms.
- Increase overseas aid to 1% of GNI and climate finance to 1.5% by 2033; contribute to Loss and Damage; support ecocide law; expand debt relief and technology transfer to the Global South.
